name: AWS AppFabric
oneLiner: Per authorised user per month, plus a small monthly add-on per user for each app beyond thirty.
trap: The meter counts users in the connected SaaS applications, not the security people reading the output, so one large SaaS tenant sets the price. The audit logs it delivers are stored and queried at your own cost.

name: AWS Audit Manager
oneLiner: Per resource assessment, where one assessment is one piece of evidence about one resource.
trap: A daily config snapshot across a hundred instances is a hundred assessments a day, not one, and the Config and Security Hub checks feeding evidence bill on their own. Closed to new customers since April 30, 2026.

name: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM)
oneLiner: Public certificates you terminate on AWS are free. Exporting one, ACME, or an Amazon N2 mTLS cert is not.
trap: Only non-exportable public certs on integrated AWS services are free. Exportable, ACME and Amazon N2 certs bill per domain name at issuance and every renewal, N2 even on AWS services, wildcards far higher.

name: Amazon Cloud Directory
oneLiner: Per GB-month of directory data, plus per-request charges split by read consistency.
trap: Writes and strongly consistent reads share the expensive request tier while eventually consistent reads sit in the cheap one, so a consistency flag decides the bill. Closed to new customers since November 7, 2025.

name: AWS CloudHSM
oneLiner: Rent an HSM by the hour. Whatever crypto you run on it is unmetered.
trap: No per-operation charge exists, so the only lever is HSM count and uptime. A production HA cluster needs at least two, and the clock keeps running on an idle HSM until you delete it.

name: Amazon Cognito
oneLiner: User pools bill per monthly active user. Machine-to-machine tokens sit on a separate per-request meter.
trap: Identity pools are free; user pools are not. M2M token requests never count as MAUs and app clients are free. Multi-Region replication adds a fee on every MAU, failover or not. Lite to Essentials reprices every user.

name: AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities
oneLiner: A monthly fee per line of code under protection, plus inference units for the security work Continuum performs.
trap: The context fee bills on lines of code connected, not on findings, so a clean repository still costs every month. The free trial covers Continuum penetration testing only, not code vulnerabilities.

name: Amazon Detective
oneLiner: One meter. GB of log and finding data ingested, per account, per Region, per month.
trap: There is no per-account or per-graph fee, so the bill tracks GuardDuty and VPC flow log volume. Widen GuardDuty coverage and Detective grows with it. A free trial hides the real number for a month.

name: AWS Directory Service
oneLiner: Every domain controller bills by the hour from creation to deletion, idle or not.
trap: The console shows one directory; the bill counts domain controllers, and Managed Microsoft AD runs at least two. Sharing to another account adds its own hourly charge, and multi-Region replication bills per GB out.

name: AWS Firewall Manager
oneLiner: Per policy, per Region, per month. Whatever the policy deploys bills separately at full price.
trap: You pay the policy fee and full price for the WAF ACLs, Network Firewall endpoints and Config rules it rolls out. Shield Advanced subscribers get the policy fee waived but still pay for Config.

name: Amazon GuardDuty
oneLiner: Priced on what it reads: per CloudTrail event, per GB of log data analyzed, per vCPU-month of runtime agent.
trap: The per-GB meter counts log volume analyzed, so keeping traffic inside the VPC saves nothing. With Security Hub on in the same account and Region, the runtime vCPU charge moves onto the Security Hub bill.

name: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
oneLiner: Free. Users, roles, policies, MFA, all of it.
trap: IAM itself never bills. Access Analyzer is the part that does, and it is a separate entry: unused-access and internal-access analysers charge per monitored resource per month.

name: AWS IAM Access Analyzer
oneLiner: External access findings are free; unused and internal access analysers bill per monitored resource a month.
trap: Switching on an unused access analyser meters every IAM role and user in the account every month, and a second analyser over the same account bills those resources again. Custom policy checks are charged per API call.

name: AWS IAM Identity Center
oneLiner: Permission sets, the access portal and SSO into your accounts are all free. The identity source behind them may not be.
trap: AWS Managed Microsoft AD as the identity source bills per domain controller hour, and a managed directory runs two of them. An external IdP or the built-in directory keeps the whole path at zero.

name: AWS IAM Roles Anywhere
oneLiner: No charge for the service. The CA it trusts is usually the expensive half.
trap: With AWS Private CA as the trust anchor you rent the CA monthly and pay again per certificate issued. Registering a CA from your own PKI as the trust anchor costs nothing anywhere along the path.

name: Amazon Inspector
oneLiner: EC2, AMIs and Lambda meter by the hour of coverage. Container images and code repos meter per scan.
trap: ECR bills per assessment, so a CI pipeline pushing all day pays for every initial scan and every rescan of every image. EC2 and Lambda coverage prorates by instance-hour, so short-lived hosts cost little.

name: AWS IoT Device Defender
oneLiner: Audit bills per device per month. Detect bills per metric datapoint reported, not per device.
trap: ML Detect costs up to eighty times Rules Detect per datapoint, about five times at scale, and bills through its two-week training window. Detect is closed to new customers since August 31, 2026.

name: AWS Key Management Service (KMS)
oneLiner: Two meters running together. A monthly fee per customer-managed key, and a charge on every cryptographic call.
trap: AWS managed keys cost nothing to store, but requests against them still bill. Rotation adds a key-month for the first and second rotation only. Cross-account, the caller pays, not the key owner.

name: AWS License Manager
oneLiner: No charge of its own.
trap: License Manager adds nothing to the bill. What catches people out is the infrastructure it steers you toward, such as EC2 Dedicated Hosts for BYOL enforcement, which bill at full per-host hourly rates.

name: Amazon Macie
oneLiner: A small daily charge per S3 bucket to keep the inventory, then per GB whenever objects get inspected.
trap: Inventory is cheap and sensitive data discovery is not. One targeted job over a large bucket can outrun a year of monitoring, and the GB counted is data scanned inside S3, nothing to do with transfer.

name: AWS Network Firewall
oneLiner: An hourly fee for each firewall endpoint in each AZ, plus a per-GB charge on inspected traffic.
trap: Endpoints are billed per AZ, so a three-AZ VPC runs three hourly meters before any traffic flows. The per-GB fee is on traffic processed by the firewall, which includes traffic that never leaves AWS.

name: AWS Network Security Manager
oneLiner: An hourly fee per account per Region where policies exist, plus an hourly fee per protected asset per firewall.
trap: The account fee runs every hour a policy exists, even one guarding a single load balancer. The WAF and Shield Advanced protections it deploys bill at their own rates, and an asset behind both pays the asset fee twice.

name: AWS Payment Cryptography
oneLiner: A monthly charge per active key, prorated hourly, plus a per-call charge on every API operation.
trap: A key bills from the moment its state goes complete, whether or not a transaction ever touches it, and the per-call rate stays high until you clear twenty million calls in a month.

name: AWS Private Certificate Authority
oneLiner: You rent the CA by the month even when it issues nothing, and pay again per certificate.
trap: The monthly CA fee starts at creation. Delete a CA and restore it inside the 7-to-30-day window and you are billed for the gap. Short-lived certificate mode costs a fraction of general-purpose mode.

name: AWS Resource Access Manager
oneLiner: Free. The shared resource still bills its owner.
trap: Sharing is free but ownership is not. Whoever owns the transit gateway or subnet keeps paying for it, and consumers pay their own usage, so a resource share moves cost around and never removes it.

name: AWS Secrets Manager
oneLiner: Storing a secret costs a flat monthly fee. Reading it costs a little more each time.
trap: Uncached GetSecretValue on every request is the usual blowup. Each replica, in another Region or now another account, bills as a full secret, and the fee runs whether the secret is read or not.

name: AWS Continuum for Penetration Testing (formerly AWS Security Agent)
oneLiner: Per task-hour of autonomous penetration testing. Task-hours accumulate across parallel work.
trap: Task-hours are cumulative, not wall clock: a pen test that finishes in four hours can bill twenty-four task-hours because the agent works in parallel. Revalidations past the third per finding bill too.

name: AWS Security Hub
oneLiner: Charged per monitored resource unit per month. Threat Analytics meters separately on events, logs and runtime vCPUs.
trap: Resource units are weighted very unevenly. One EC2 instance or Azure or GCP VM is a whole unit while it takes about a dozen Lambda functions or over a hundred IAM identities to reach the same unit.

name: AWS Security Incident Response
oneLiner: Per security finding ingested from GuardDuty and Security Hub, past a monthly free allowance.
trap: Findings ingested drive the bill, not incidents you actually escalate, so a chatty detection integration is what costs you. The first 10,000 a month are free, and Enterprise Support and Unified Operations pay nothing.

name: Amazon Security Lake
oneLiner: Per GB of log data delivered into the lake, plus a separate per-GB charge to normalize it to OCSF.
trap: CloudTrail events ingest at triple the rate of other sources, and normalization bills on top of ingestion. The S3 storage, Glue, EventBridge, Lambda and SQS under the lake are all billed separately.

name: AWS Shield (Standard and Advanced)
oneLiner: Standard is free and always on. Advanced is a subscription plus per-GB data transfer out of protected resources.
trap: Advanced needs a one-year commitment and bills once per payer account covering the whole organization. Data transfer out of CloudFront, ELB, EC2 and Global Accelerator then meters on top of the subscription.

name: AWS Security Token Service (STS)
oneLiner: Call AssumeRole and GetCallerIdentity as hard as you like. The STS line on your bill stays at zero.
trap: Every STS call is a CloudTrail management event. A tight AssumeRole loop costs nothing at STS and shows up as real money in GuardDuty event analysis and in any trail beyond your first.

name: AWS Verified Access
oneLiner: Each application endpoint runs an hourly meter, and the traffic through it bills per GB.
trap: The hourly fee attaches to each application, not to the Verified Access instance, so fifty apps means fifty meters. Normal AWS data transfer charges land on top of the data-processing fee.

name: Amazon Verified Permissions
oneLiner: Every authorization decision is a billed API request, and policy reads and writes bill too.
trap: A BatchIsAuthorized call meters as one request however many decisions it carries, but costs thirty times a lone IsAuthorized, so batching only pays off once you pack it full. ListPolicies bills as well.

name: AWS WAF
oneLiner: Per web ACL and rule a month plus per request, until February 2027. Then per protected resource-hour plus per request.
trap: From February 1, 2027 web ACL, rule and rule group fees go, but every associated resource bills hourly, so one ACL on fifty load balancers is fifty meters. Premium rule groups add a per-request fee on top.
